name: Foundation Building
purpose: Establish learner understanding with clearly relevant dev data. Should trigger multiple syntheses.
items: Spent 3 hours debugging a race condition in our WebSocket handler. Two async ops modifying the same connection map simultaneously. Added a mutex lock around the critical section.
Refactored the auth middleware — split monolithic validateToken() into parseToken(), verifySignature(), and checkExpiry(). Each independently testable now.
API response times jumped from 50ms to 800ms after new search feature. Found N+1 queries — one DB hit per result for tags. Batch query brought it back to 60ms.
Pairing session on the caching layer. Chose write-through over write-behind. More consistent, slightly slower writes. Consistency wins for our use case.
Test suite takes 14 minutes. 60% is integration tests spinning up real DB containers. Looking into test database pooling or in-memory alternatives.
Implemented retry logic for external API calls. Exponential backoff with jitter: 100ms base, max 3 retries, 2x multiplier, random jitter up to 50%.
PR review took 3 days for a 20-line change. Only two people can approve. Need to distribute review ownership across the team.
Switched from REST to GraphQL for mobile API. Mobile team was making 5-6 requests per screen. Now one query. Network payload dropped 70%.
Spent morning writing docs for the event system. Found naming is inconsistent — past tense, present, nouns mixed. Standardizing to past tense.
Worker queue error handling too aggressive — retries indefinitely on any failure. Malformed payloads get stuck in infinite loops. Added dead letter queue after 5 failures.
Deployed first canary release. 5% traffic to new version, monitored 2 hours, gradually increased to 100%. Zero incidents.
Database migration tool doesn't support rollbacks for ALTER TABLE. Had to write manual down migration. Every migration should be reversible.
Found memory leak in Node.js service. Event listeners added in request handler without removal. After 10k requests, thousands of orphaned listeners.
Team agreed on trunk-based development with short-lived feature branches. No more long-running develop branch. PRs under 400 lines.
Implemented structured logging across all services. Every entry: timestamp, service name, trace ID, severity, structured context.
Dependency audit: 847 direct deps, 3200+ transitive. Found 3 packages unchanged in 4 years with known vulns. Started audit process.
Frontend team wants cursor-based pagination. They've been using offset/limit which breaks when items are inserted during pagination.
DNS change propagated faster than expected, routing prod traffic to staging DB. Root cause: shared DNS zone. Lesson: isolate infrastructure fully.
Optimized Docker images. Node.js service was 1.2GB. Multi-stage build + Alpine + pruning dev deps → 180MB. Build time 8min → 2min.
Feature flags via simple hot-reloadable JSON config. For 8 devs, this is sufficient. Don't need LaunchDarkly complexity yet.
Monorepo migration paying off. Shared types between frontend/backend catch contract mismatches at compile time. Cross-project refactoring: days → hours.
94% of errors last month from 3 root causes: payment provider timeout, invalid UTF-8 in user input, stale cache entries. Fixing these would eliminate most noise.
Designed notification data model with event sourcing. Every state change is immutable event. Current state = fold over event stream. Trivial to add channels later.
Query builder (Kysely) over ORM. Type safety and composability without full ORM abstraction penalty. Generated SQL is predictable.
Load test: 500 concurrent connections, 10s ramp. P50=45ms, P95=120ms, P99=340ms. P99 spike from cold DB connections. Adding pool warming.
Built internal CLI for feature flags, migrations, test seeding. Single binary, no runtime deps. Saving 20min per dev per day.
Added security scan as 5th CI stage. Found 2 SQL injection vulns in legacy code the linter missed. Fixed immediately.
TypeScript strict mode on shared library caught 23 type errors silently failing. Most were optional chaining on values assumed present.
First ADR: why PostgreSQL over MongoDB. Written record of decisions helps new team members understand the 'why'.
Graceful shutdown: on SIGTERM stop accepting connections, finish in-flight requests (30s timeout), flush logs, close DB pool, exit.
Investigating why our connection pool exhausts under load. Each request holds a connection for the full transaction. Switching to connection-per-query with explicit transactions only when needed.
Set up GitHub Actions with matrix builds. Testing against Node 18, 20, and 22. Found a regression in our stream handling on Node 22 — Buffer.from behavior changed subtly.
Code review checklist: 1) Does it handle errors? 2) Are there tests? 3) Is it backwards compatible? 4) Will it scale to 10x current load? Simple but catches most issues.
Implemented circuit breaker for the payment gateway. After 5 failures in 30 seconds, open the circuit for 60 seconds. Prevents cascade failures during payment provider outages.
Profiled our JSON serialization. Turns out JSON.stringify on our largest response object takes 12ms. Switched to a streaming serializer for responses >100KB.
The intern found a bug nobody else caught: we were using == instead of === in a critical auth check. String '0' was truthy-matching with number 0. Classic JS footgun.
Migrated from callbacks to async/await in the legacy notification module. 400 lines of callback hell → 150 lines of readable async code. 3 bugs fixed automatically by the simplification.
Database indexes audit. Found 6 unused indexes costing write performance and 2 missing indexes causing full table scans on the dashboard query. Net improvement: dashboard loads 5x faster.
Implemented request deduplication. Identical API calls within 100ms window return the same promise. Eliminated the double-click problem and reduced redundant DB queries by 30%.
Set up smoke tests that run after every production deploy. Hit 5 critical endpoints, verify response shape and status codes. Caught a broken deploy within 45 seconds last week.
Spent a day understanding our Webpack config. 800 lines, 14 plugins, 3 loaders nobody remembers adding. Simplified to 200 lines. Build time cut in half.
Wrote a migration to add soft deletes to the user table. Added deleted_at column, updated all queries to filter, added a cleanup job for records older than 90 days.
Our WebSocket reconnection logic was naive — reconnect immediately on disconnect. Under load, 10k clients reconnecting simultaneously DDoS'd our own server. Added jittered exponential backoff.
Implemented rate limiting with a sliding window algorithm. 100 requests per minute per user. Redis-backed for distributed consistency across 4 API servers.
Found that our test fixtures were sharing mutable state between tests. Tests passed individually but failed when run together. Switched to factory functions that create fresh data per test.
Set up database read replicas. Write queries go to primary, read queries to replicas. Dashboard response time dropped from 2s to 200ms by offloading analytics queries.
Implemented API versioning via URL path (/v1/, /v2/). Header-based versioning is cleaner but harder to test and debug. Explicit paths are boring but work.

Added structured error codes to all API responses. Instead of 'Something went wrong', now return { code: 'PAYMENT_DECLINED', message: '...', details: {...} }. Frontend can handle errors programmatically.
Our S3 upload was loading entire files into memory. For a 500MB file, that's a 500MB memory spike. Switched to streaming upload with multipart. Memory stays flat regardless of file size.
Wrote a database seeder that generates realistic test data. 10k users, 50k orders, 200k events. Takes 30 seconds. Everyone on the team can now reproduce production-like scenarios locally.
Discovered our JWT tokens never expire in development. Turns out someone set the expiry to 999 days in the .env.development file 2 years ago. Fixed to 1 hour, matching production.
Implemented webhook retry with idempotency keys. Each webhook delivery has a unique ID. Recipients can deduplicate. We retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff.
The frontend bundle is 2.4MB. Code-splitting reduced initial load to 400KB. Lazy-loaded routes for admin, settings, and reports. First meaningful paint: 3.2s → 1.1s.
Added health check endpoint that validates DB connection, Redis connection, and disk space. Load balancer removes unhealthy instances within 10 seconds.
Our email templates were hardcoded HTML strings in the codebase. Moved to MJML templates with preview capability. Designers can now iterate without deploying code.
Implemented audit logging for all admin actions. Every create/update/delete on sensitive resources gets a timestamped, immutable log entry with the acting user's ID.
Found that our cron jobs were running on all 4 instances simultaneously. Added leader election with Redis SETNX. Only one instance runs crons at a time.
Upgraded from Express to Fastify. Same API structure, 2x throughput on our benchmark. The schema-based validation is a nice bonus — catches bad requests before they hit our code.
Implemented database query timeout. Any query running longer than 5 seconds gets killed. Prevents a single slow query from exhausting the connection pool.
Set up a local development proxy that mirrors production API responses. New developers can work on frontend features without spinning up the entire backend stack.
Wrote a pre-commit hook that runs TypeScript type checking on changed files only. Full type check takes 45 seconds; incremental takes 3 seconds. No more excuses to skip it.

Implemented graceful degradation for our third-party analytics. If the analytics service is down, we buffer events locally and replay when it comes back. Core functionality never blocked by analytics.
Our GraphQL schema had 200+ types but no documentation. Added descriptions to every type, field, and argument. GraphQL Playground is now self-documenting.
Discovered we were making 12 Redis round-trips per request. Pipelined them into 2 batched calls. Response time for the worst endpoint: 180ms → 45ms.
Implemented content-based cache invalidation. Instead of TTL-based expiry, we hash the query parameters and invalidate when the underlying data changes. Cache hit rate went from 60% to 92%.
Set up error grouping in our monitoring tool. Instead of 10,000 individual error alerts, we now see 15 error groups ranked by frequency and impact. Actionable instead of overwhelming.
Added request tracing headers that propagate through our entire stack: API → queue → worker → database. Can now trace a single user action across all services.
Our password hashing was using MD5. Migrated to bcrypt with cost factor 12. Added a migration that re-hashes passwords on next login. Old hashes expire after 90 days.
Implemented blue-green deployments. Two identical environments, traffic switches instantly via load balancer. Rollback is flipping traffic back. Zero downtime deploys.
Found our ORM was generating SELECT * on every query. Switched to explicit column selection. Reduced network transfer by 40% on our largest table (30 columns, only 5 needed).
Wrote integration tests for our payment flow: create order → process payment → handle webhook → update order status. Catches regressions that unit tests miss.
Implemented connection draining on deploy. Old instances finish their in-flight requests (up to 30s) before shutting down. No more 502 errors during deployments.
Our development database was 50GB of production data from a year ago. Created a minimal seed with 1000 records per table. Dev environment starts in 5 seconds instead of 5 minutes.
Added OpenAPI spec generation from our route definitions. API documentation is always in sync with code. Generated TypeScript client for the frontend automatically.
Implemented distributed locking for our scheduled report generation. Two instances were generating the same report simultaneously, sending duplicate emails to customers.
Set up synthetic monitoring — automated tests that run every 5 minutes against production, simulating real user flows. We know about outages before customers report them.
Found a subtle timezone bug: we were storing timestamps as local time in some places and UTC in others. Standardized everything to UTC with explicit timezone conversion at display layer.
Implemented streaming responses for our export endpoint. Previously loaded 100k records into memory to generate CSV. Now stream rows directly. Memory usage: 500MB → 20MB.
Our API authentication was checking permissions on every request by querying the database. Added a 5-minute permission cache per user. Auth overhead: 15ms → 0.5ms for cached requests.
Created a runbook for common incidents: database failover, cache invalidation, rolling back deployments, scaling up workers. On-call engineers can now resolve issues in minutes instead of hours.
Implemented feature flag gradual rollout. New feature goes to 1% of users → 10% → 50% → 100% over 4 days. If error rate spikes at any stage, auto-rollback.
Our test suite was flaky — 3 tests failed randomly due to timing issues. Root cause: tests depended on setTimeout ordering. Replaced with deterministic event-driven assertions.
Added a database query analyzer to our CI pipeline. Any new query without an index gets flagged. Caught 2 potential full table scans before they reached production.
Implemented per-tenant rate limiting. Enterprise customers get 10x the rate limit of free tier. Stored in Redis sorted sets for O(1) lookups.
Our error messages were developer-oriented: 'TypeError: Cannot read property x of undefined'. Added user-friendly error mapping: technical error → human-readable message per context.
Set up automated dependency updates with Renovate. PRs created weekly for minor/patch updates, monthly for majors. Each PR runs full test suite. Merged 80% automatically.
Implemented cursor-based pagination with opaque cursors. Encodes (id, timestamp) as base64. Consistent results even when data changes between pages.
Found that our logger was synchronously writing to stdout, blocking the event loop for 2ms per log line under high load. Switched to async buffered logging. P99 dropped by 15ms.
Created a chaos testing schedule: kill a random pod (Mon), introduce 200ms network latency (Wed), fail a database replica (Fri). Each test has a runbook and expected recovery time.
Our session store was in-memory. When a server restarted, all users got logged out. Migrated to Redis-backed sessions. Sessions survive restarts and work across all instances.
Implemented API request signing for webhooks. HMAC-SHA256 signature in the header. Recipients verify the signature to ensure the request came from us and wasn't tampered with.
Optimized our full-text search by switching from LIKE queries to PostgreSQL tsvector. Search across 1M records: 2.3s → 45ms. Added GIN index on the tsvector column.
Set up automated backups with point-in-time recovery. Full backup nightly, WAL archiving every 5 minutes. Can restore to any point in the last 30 days.
Our worker processes were single-threaded. Introduced worker clustering with Node.js cluster module. CPU utilization went from 25% to 90% on our 4-core instances.
Implemented request validation middleware. Every endpoint has a Zod schema. Invalid requests get rejected with detailed error messages before reaching business logic.
Found we were logging sensitive data — user emails and partial credit card numbers in error traces. Added a log sanitizer that masks PII fields before writing.
Created a PR template with checkboxes: tests added, docs updated, migration reversible, no breaking changes, security review if auth-related. Reduced review back-and-forth by 50%.
Our CI pipeline downloads dependencies fresh every run. Added npm cache between builds. Pipeline time: 12 minutes → 7 minutes. Cache hit rate: 95%.
Implemented API deprecation headers. Deprecated endpoints return Sunset and Deprecation headers with the removal date. Clients have 6 months to migrate.
Set up log aggregation with structured JSON logs → Elasticsearch → Kibana. Can now search across all services with complex queries. Debugging distributed issues went from hours to minutes.
Our database connection string was hardcoded in 7 different files. Centralized to a single config module that reads from environment variables. Changed once, applied everywhere.
Implemented progressive image loading. Thumbnails load instantly (2KB), full images load on scroll. Initial page load time for image-heavy pages: 8s → 1.5s.
Found that our test database wasn't being cleaned between test files. Tests were polluting each other's data. Added per-file database transactions that rollback after each test.
Set up GitHub Dependabot security alerts. Got 12 alerts on first scan. All were in dev dependencies except one critical vulnerability in a production XML parser. Patched within an hour.
